newsitem.title: USA: Crown workers picket Texas refinery.
newsitem.headline: Crown workers picket Texas refinery.

text.p: Workers rallied outside the gates of Crown Central Petroleum Corp's Pasadena, Texas refinery on Wednesday to mark the one-year anniversary of a union lock-out at the plant, union and refinery officials said.

Little progress has been made over the past year to reach a new three-year labor pact and end the lock-out, which started after company officials discovered equipment vandalized at the 100,000 barrel per day refinery.

"They are essentially at the same place they were a year ago," Tom Gentry, president of the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Local 4-227, said of the talks. Negotiations were set to resume on Monday with a federal mediator.
Crown and its union workers have been at odds over the company's plans to cut the refinery's 270-person workforce and ignore seniority in replacing some union workers with contractors.
Crown managers and contractors have operated the refinery since the lock-out, an arrangement a spokesman for the Baltimore-based company said could continue "indefinitely."
The union rally started at 1610 CST, exactly one year to the minute since workers were ushered out the gates of the Houston-area refinery, Gentry said.
